<!-- pr-reviewer: f35f0ff88c21e7df2bf243be5d1e1aa4a5907097 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thanks, austin62jake - tidy, small, and it reuses the GUI's own command rather than adding a second path.

**What looks good**
- Everything Is a Command: `crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs:42-43` builds `MoveModel::new(...)` and runs it through `env.history.execute(...)`, the same undoable command the GUI issues. No direct component writes; undo/redo of part and followed stock is pinned in `a_moved_part_carries_a_one_part_documents_stock_and_one_undo_puts_both_back`.
- Refusals by name, validated at command creation: all of `MoveModel::new`'s own text (fixture, work offset, machine table, unknown name, non-quaternion via `check_location`) is returned as a tool error, plus `"position" is required` / a wrong-length position from `opt_nums`. `move_model_refuses_by_name_and_a_refusal_enters_no_history` checks none enters History.
- `MoveModel::following_stock()` (`commands/move_model.rs:192`) is a read-only accessor; no behaviour change to the command. No unwrap/expect/panic, no casts or indexing added.
- Layering fine (all in app); new file has module doc plus a `Provenance:` line, 68 lines; decision file `docs/decisions/716-mcp-move-model.md` present; body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #716`; no CHANGELOG.md edit; no deps, build.rs, scripts or .github.

**Local results (merged with current upstream/main, no conflicts; fresh target dir)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `mcp_model` | 3 passed |
| `mcp` | 13 passed |
| `mcp_live` | 10 passed |
| `mcp_setup` | 6 passed |
| `mcp_pick` | 2 passed |
| `mcp_pockets` | 3 passed |
| `mcp_render` | 5 passed |
| `camcraft-app --lib` | 107 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `pose_of` falls back to the default (identity) location when an entity has no transform; that only affects the reply for a name that already passed `MoveModel::new`, so it cannot mask a refusal.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's gaps list is correctly left for a process-version change.
- `feat(app)`: ships at the next minor cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
